Task: faithful HD remaster of a sheet of animation frames from the 1993 adventure game Sam & Max Hit the Road (LucasArts). This is a production asset. Every frame replaces one original frame in the game, at the same size and position, and the frames are played one after another.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged exactly 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat magenta background (#FF00FF). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The background and the border are only padding.

What the sheet shows: Sam, the dog detective (a big brown dog in a light blue-gray suit, white shirt, striped dark blue tie and a blue-gray fedora). The description is only a help; the input image decides. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: start pose, facing right (17 frames). The game mirrors the frames facing right when the character faces left, so there are no frames facing left; do not add any.

Size rule (most important): draw every frame at exactly the size it has in the input, with the same height, the same width and the same proportions of head, body, arms, legs and props. One input pixel is 4 output pixels for every frame on this sheet and on every other sheet of this character, so the character never grows, shrinks or changes shape between frames. On this sheet the frames are from 272 to 280 pixels tall and from 156 to 224 pixels wide in the input (the box around each frame's visible pixels); jobb.json lists every frame's box under ruter (synlig, in original pixels: multiply by 4).

Do:
- Trace every frame at 4x in high resolution, so it looks like the characters of Day of the Tentacle Remastered next to their originals: keep the pose, silhouette and proportions, and turn every cluster of pixels into the shape it shows (glasses, a tie, a shoe). Clean dark anti-aliased outlines with a little variation in weight, flat colors with one shade and a few highlights, the same color for every area as in the input. No dithering, no texture, no gradients, no pixel steps.
- Keep the original design: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast as in the input.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, eyes, hat, clothes, colors and light in every frame. Any difference between frames flickers in the game.
- Keep the pose and silhouette of every frame, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, lightning, sparks, fire) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge, split or redesign frames.
- Do not add anything that is not in the input: no new props, accessories, patterns, logos, text, shadows, floor, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not change colors, clothes or proportions, and do not make heads, hands or eyes bigger than in the input.
- Some frames show only part of the character (a body without a head, a head alone, an arm), because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha: no background color and no gray border) and every frame in the same place as in the input. Before delivering, run python3 verktoy/sjekk_leveranse.py jobber/fig272_01/resultat.png and redo the frames it reports as too big, too small, moved or missing. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing, alpha above 128).

If a second image is attached, it is the approved master sheet (hovedark) of this character, or an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take every pose, size and position from the first image. If a third image is attached, it is the master sheet of the second character on the sheet.


SCOPED SOURCE CLARIFICATION: Produce ONLY the 6 distinct Sam poses in attached source contact sheet, in its exact 3 column by 2 row order, remaining cells empty. This is a re-layout of original source cels, not the final atlas. Preserve each source pose exactly: SAME brown dog Sam, blue gray suit and fedora, white shirt, dark blue diagonally striped tie. Source-specific head angle, eyes, closed mouth, short legs and long horizontal snout take precedence over style sheet. All feet are bare brown dog paws, NOT shoes. Match the Sam style reference only for clean hand ink and restrained flat cel shading, not its neutral pose. Do NOT make the head larger or the legs longer. Preserve hand-object contact and source-specific mouth differences. Generate a clean RGBA transparent sprite sheet, no magenta, gray or floor shadows, no text, no numbered labels. We will scale whole NEW components to their original source boxes, never warp them. VORTEX context: The orange/yellow shallow disk with blue underside is a HAND-HELD VORTEX, not food. Retain its tiny colored components and the disappearance fragments where visible, without adding a glow or particles.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged exactly 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat magenta background (#FF00FF). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The background and the border are only padding.

What the sheet shows: Sam, the dog detective (a big brown dog in a light blue-gray suit, white shirt, striped dark blue tie and a blue-gray fedora). The description is only a help; the input image decides. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: animation 7, facing right (13 frames). The game mirrors the frames facing right when the character faces left, so there are no frames facing left; do not add any.

Size rule (most important): draw every frame at exactly the size it has in the input, with the same height, the same width and the same proportions of head, body, arms, legs and props. One input pixel is 4 output pixels for every frame on this sheet and on every other sheet of this character, so the character never grows, shrinks or changes shape between frames. On this sheet the frames are from 272 to 280 pixels tall and from 152 to 220 pixels wide in the input (the box around each frame's visible pixels); jobb.json lists every frame's box under ruter (synlig, in original pixels: multiply by 4).

Do:
- Trace every frame at 4x in high resolution, so it looks like the characters of Day of the Tentacle Remastered next to their originals: keep the pose, silhouette and proportions, and turn every cluster of pixels into the shape it shows (glasses, a tie, a shoe). Clean dark anti-aliased outlines with a little variation in weight, flat colors with one shade and a few highlights, the same color for every area as in the input. No dithering, no texture, no gradients, no pixel steps.
- Keep the original design: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast as in the input.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, eyes, hat, clothes, colors and light in every frame. Any difference between frames flickers in the game.
- Keep the pose and silhouette of every frame, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, lightning, sparks, fire) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge, split or redesign frames.
- Do not add anything that is not in the input: no new props, accessories, patterns, logos, text, shadows, floor, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not change colors, clothes or proportions, and do not make heads, hands or eyes bigger than in the input.
- Some frames show only part of the character (a body without a head, a head alone, an arm), because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha: no background color and no gray border) and every frame in the same place as in the input. Before delivering, run python3 verktoy/sjekk_leveranse.py jobber/fig272_03/resultat.png and redo the frames it reports as too big, too small, moved or missing. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing, alpha above 128).

If a second image is attached, it is the approved master sheet (hovedark) of this character, or an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take every pose, size and position from the first image. If a third image is attached, it is the master sheet of the second character on the sheet.


SCOPED SOURCE CLARIFICATION: Produce ONLY the 5 distinct Sam poses in attached source contact sheet, in its exact 3 column by 2 row order, remaining cells empty. This is a re-layout of original source cels, not the final atlas. Preserve each source pose exactly: SAME brown dog Sam, blue gray suit and fedora, white shirt, dark blue diagonally striped tie. Source-specific head angle, eyes, closed mouth, short legs and long horizontal snout take precedence over style sheet. All feet are bare brown dog paws, NOT shoes. Match the Sam style reference only for clean hand ink and restrained flat cel shading, not its neutral pose. Do NOT make the head larger or the legs longer. Preserve hand-object contact and source-specific mouth differences. Generate a clean RGBA transparent sprite sheet, no magenta, gray or floor shadows, no text, no numbered labels. We will scale whole NEW components to their original source boxes, never warp them. TANN context: The small curved ivory object is a DINOSAUR TOOTH held in the hand, tip down then tilted horizontally; it is not a knife, cone or food. Keep its original bend and extent. Empty-hand poses stay empty.
EXACT DENTAL SHAPE: Every tooth has ONE pointed end and ONE BLUNT broad flat or gently rounded root. NO second pointed hook at the top/right root. FIRST pose: point downward below fist, broad BLUNT IVORY ROOT above fist. SECOND and THIRD: single long point points LEFT under the hand, broad BLUNT IVORY ROOT projects to RIGHT above fist. No blade, no horns, no point on root, no metal, no gold or blue trim. Source geometry decides; keep the white parts exactly as shown.
